built_on: user's Docker Desktop (macOS), not the Claude authoring sandbox (no Docker there)
build_command: fprime-util generate && fprime-util build (Ref reference deployment, framework's own tool suite from requirements.txt)
smoke_test_result: Ref binary launched, rejected an unrecognized --help flag with a real usage message ('-a hostname/IP address', '-p port_number') confirming a genuine, working F´ deployment executable, not a stub
reproducibility_note: Independently verified 2026-08-03: a second, from-scratch Docker rebuild (`docker build --no-cache`, ~1 hour after the first) of the Ref binary produced a byte-for-byte identical artifact — sha256 e271e22c37d11d3b27f03b0d033291af727e4d11f8bdffa1c6a8aa83b47f4b9b matched exactly, `cmp -l` reported 0 differing bytes. This is a genuine two-independent-builds comparison, not the trivial copy-integrity check `build.py` performs per pipeline call (see its module docstring) — see docs/Threat-Model.md 'Phase 7 reproducibility verification' for full methodology and STATUS.md 'Claims status' for exactly what this does and doesn't license claiming. Contrast with cfs-app/confirmed-build.json, whose real cFS build was NOT bit-identical across the same test.
known_limitation: The Ref binary is a network server (waits for a GDS connection via -a/-p, retrying forever if none is present), not a short-lived deterministic CLI program. Resolved (ISSUES-AND-FIXES-LOG.md ISSUE-003): src/health/health_check.py now uses a persistent-process strategy for this stack — launches the binary with a placeholder -a/-p, watches stdout for the real 'Hit Ctrl-C to quit' log line (printed before any network activity) within a bounded window, then terminates it — so S3+ conditions (attestation, health check, rollback) can be exercised against this real binary. Individual test runs pass; a repeated-trial statistical evaluation against this real binary has not yet been done (still PRELIMINARY_INTERNAL_ONLY per STATUS.md).
